summary: Crystalline SrZrO3 was deposited on Ge (001) using atomic layer deposition (ALD) for high-k dielectric applications. The process involved pretreatment of Ge (001) with 0.5-monolayers of Ba and growth of SrZrO3 using strontium bis(triisopropylcyclopentadienyl), tetrakis (dimethylamido) zirconium, and water at 225 °C. The films were crystallized at 590 °C, and post-deposition annealing was avoided. The films showed a dielectric constant of 30, leakage current density of 2.1 × 10⁻⁸ A/cm² at 1 MV/cm, and an equivalent oxide thickness of 0.8 nm. Oxygen plasma pretreatment and atomic deuterium post-treatment were used to reduce interface trap density.
evidence: Crystalline SrZrO3 deposition on Ge (001) by atomic layer deposition for high-k dielectric applications. Ge (001) surfaces are pretreated with 0.5-monolayers (ML) of Ba and an amorphous /C24 3-nm SZO layer is grown from strontium bis(triisopropylcyclopentadienyl), tetrakis (dimethylamido) zirconium, and water at 225 /C14 C. This /C24 3-nm layer crystallizes at 590 /C14 C and subsequent SZO growth at 225 /C14 C leads to crystalline films that do not require further annealing. The film properties are investigated using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, x-ray diffraction, aberration-corrected electron microscopy, and capacitance-voltage measurements of metal-oxide semiconductor capacitor structures. Capacitance-voltage measurements of the SrZrO3/Ge heterojunctions reveal a dielectric constant of 30 for SrZrO3 and a leakage current density of 2.1 /C2 10/C0 8 A/cm2 at 1 MV/cm with an equivalent oxide thickness of 0.8 nm. Oxygen plasma pretreatment of Ge (001), Zintl layer formation with 0.5 ML Ba, and atomic deuterium post-growth treatment were explored to lower interface trap density (Dit) and achieved a Dit of 8.56 /C2 1011 cm/C0 2 eV/C0 1.
